Deferred with the line it rests on. | Deferred |
| [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) v2 | Translation may preserve local meanings while changing the global structure of meaning: reconstruction can keep most local judgements and change their global compatibility | A78's thesis for the paper, "potentially the most interesting connection we've found", with Δ_CF, the change in contextual fraction along a chain, as its measure. Dropped at outline v3 without critique. | Proposed |

Dropped when the latents were demoted at U28, without critique. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-122](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-122.md) | Will-organization is not one more higher-order preference: changing the conditions of efficacy changes behaviour while the competing preferences stay fixed | The reply to [CLAIM-089](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-089.md) (Section 3.5), by precommitment in a person and escalation authority in a firm. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-123](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-123.md) | In conditional generation each condition can be met while their conjunction or relational binding fails, and adding scores composes conditions only under conditional independence at the noisy state | The manuscript's §7, citing Composable Diffusion, T2I-CompBench and Schrödinger bridges. | [CLAIM-124](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-124.md) | Communicative objects are characterized through overlapping constraints on observables at partially ordered levels; translation transports these locally constrained structures, and repeated reconstruction changes both local interpretations and their global compatibility | The thesis of proposal v5 (A81–A83, under U30), which put observational structure first: "a global communicative object is no longer stipulated in advance." What is left open is decision-relevant information and signalling data. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-126](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-126.md) | Model stitching tests whether a transport preserves decision-relevant information only in its reconstruction form: a map fitted to reproduce the target representation certifies one direction of Blackwell sufficiency, while task-loss stitching compares one decision problem through a fixed head, and a failure to stitch is no evidence against sufficiency | Proposed by the record on 2026-10-09 as an operational handle on the decision-relevant half of [CLAIM-125](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-125.md), and qualified by the reading of Bansal, Nakkiran & Barak before it was filed: only reconstruction-fitted stitching certifies sufficiency, and only within the map class. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md) v2 | Conditioning on a communicative situation, intervening on it and intervening on what the interpreter is told are three different operations, so a framing intervention should index the empirical model, e_C^a = P(Y_C \| do(a)), not enter its cover as one more context | The owner's do() move at U41, formalized at A129 §1 and §5 and restated in the review relayed the same day. A129 keeps three operations apart: conditioning on the situation, intervening on it, and intervening on what the interpreter is told. | [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) | Transports whose distortion profiles trade off are incomparable until a task fixes weights, so no single ranking of translations holds across tasks | A129 §3, after the owner's U41 "agreed." to unifying the fidelity lineages, and restated at A151 §5, A178 Ch9.7 and A203 §22. | [CLAIM-129](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-129.md) v2 | A factorization recovers only the structure visible in the relations it is fitted to, so a topic can survive a transformation that changes the communicative act, and a kind must be tested against probe families chosen for their bearing on the act | The assistant's, at A210 §5 after the owner's U58, and again at A214 §3–§4. It does not say lexical structure is irrelevant to the act, or that a richer factorization cannot capture acts. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-130](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-130.md) | Telling an interpreter about a communicative situation, do(I = a), is a different intervention from changing the situation, do(S = s), so the effect of a cue is evidence about interpretation under instruction, not about whether the act changed | The owner proposed Pearl's do() at U41, and A129 §1 drew the distinction. | [CLAIM-133](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-133.md) | Communicative identity is relational continuity under admissible transformation: translation transports relationally organized observational structure, correspondence fixes what can be compared, admissibility which transformations count, and fidelity which communicatively consequential distinctions remain recoverable | The thesis of the assistant's two consolidations after the U40–U42 review: the state of the argument at U43 (A151) and proposal outline v7 at U49 (A178). The owner asked for "the current state of our argument" and for the proposal to be updated "to account for our progress", and argued no change. Filed so that the change of thesis is visible, as [CLAIM-017](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-017.md) was. It does not replace [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), which no draft has given up, and the October thesis replaced it in turn. | Superseded — by [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) |
| [CLAIM-135](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-135.md) | Recovering latent structure from relational data is three achievements, reconstruction, identification up to stated ambiguities, and constitution of a communicative kind, and identifiability theory reaches the second at most | The assistant's, at A207 §5 (three profiles) and A214 §1 (three problems, two warrants), kept as A218 §5's five objects of inquiry. A214 asked for it as a THEORY; it is the record's own distinction, so it is a claim. It answers [QUESTION-001](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-001.md) in part, by naming a failure that question did not. | [CLAIM-136](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-136.md) | Communicative acts and their participants exist as relata but have no identity beyond what their relations differentiate: non-eliminative structural realism without primitive identity | The owner's U54 position, its second part: "Individuated objects exist, but only in so far as they are differentiated by their relata." The assistant placed it "close to" Esfeld and Lam (A194), then weakened it without saying so, from "only in so far as differentiated" to numerical plurality without differentiation (A194 §5, A198 §3, A203 §2). The owner has not chosen between the two versions. | Proposed |

It is the first owner-stated answer to [QUESTION-021](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-021.md) that takes neither horn. The assistant kept "more essential" in the sense of classificatory priority (A194 §1, A198 §I). A218 weakens it further, without argument, to "may be better guides to its kind". | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) | A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization rather than in any expression or encoding; statistical methods recover aspects of that organization from restricted observations, translation transports it, and fidelity is which independently identifiable, decision-relevant relational distinctions persist | The thesis of the assistant's second crystallized argument (A203, at U56), of A214 (U59) and of the October proposal and outline (A218, U60). No draft carries it, so it complements the manuscript's thesis rather than superseding it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md) v2 | Two communicative realizations can agree on every probe in a restricted family without being structurally identical, so observational equivalence is relative to the probes, and only independently justified probes evaluated on held-out cases are evidence that structure was preserved | It began at the owner's U45 pointer to Yoneda, and A158 §5 gave it its first form. The substantive half is the realist commitment that communicative identity is not exhausted by any probe profile. It makes [TERM-014](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-014.md)'s equivalence class probe-relative, and puts a realist reading over [CLAIM-046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-046.md)'s methodological ordering. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md) | Local descriptions that disagree are not thereby incompatible: whether there is an obstruction can be assessed only after the correspondence between their observations is fixed and independently validated | A164, after the owner's U47, restated by A173, A178, A203, A214 and A218. Three classes of disagreement (coordinate difference, structural transformation, global obstruction) and an order of tests: fix and validate the correspondence, then ask whether the descriptions extend jointly. A173 proposed it as a design principle; it is a thesis of the line. The relativity example motivates it and is not evidence for it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-147](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-147.md) | A trope is a family of observational profiles joined by admissible transformations around a core of preserved relations, so trope instances can separate structural preservation from pragmatic preservation | A155, at U44, after the owner proposed TV Tropes. Comparing such families tests whether relational measures track communicative identity where surface similarity fails. A178 made it Study B; A191 §8 gave it five manipulations. The record objects that the analysis is Propp's and Lévi-Strauss's, and that the catalogue cannot validate it ([CLAIM-145](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-145.md)). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-149](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-149.md) | A probe family that supplies a transformation's training signal cannot also certify what the transformation preserves: preservation must be shown under probes that were not used to train it | The owner set the frame at U51 ("a useful case study ... the projected GAN work"); A184 §§3–4 argued it, with its Experiment C and closing maxim, and A203 §30 and A218 Study 6 keep it. ([CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md)) is a documented instance, which the exchange did not know of. One case, in image generation, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) v2 | Which communicative act an utterance performs is partly constituted by its relations to participant roles, norms and expected uptake, so a transformation that changes those relations can change the act and not only its realization | The assistant at A187 §3, after the owner's U52 question about ontic structural realism, restated at A191 §1, A203 §3, A214 §13 and A218 §2. Searle's status functions ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) are the nearer held prior art, and "moderate OSR" is the wrong name for it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md) | Any individuation built on sufficiency is relative to the target it is sufficient for: fix the outcomes differently and a different partition wins, so no boundary drawn this way is universal | Dual-filed from [MOM-POS-001](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/positions.d/POS-001.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). A sufficient statistic is sufficient for a target Y, so every partition chosen as minimal sufficient inherits Y. MOM's example: fix the outcomes differently and "organism" wins instead of "animal". In this record it is the standing caution on every boundary criterion filed beside it ([CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md)). It does not say boundaries are arbitrary, only that each is relative to a stated target. | Active |
| [CLAIM-153](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-153.md) | Failure of a self to hold together across contexts is a monodromy around a cycle of contexts: any two locally consistent contexts glue, and the minimal model of the obstruction needs three | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-165](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-165.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Model contexts (roles, personas, sub-agents) as a cover, and the offsets that reconcile neighbours as a cochain. A global section, one coherent self, exists exactly when the monodromy Φ around a cycle vanishes. Two contexts always glue, so compartmentalization needs a loop. The frustrated XY or Kuramoto energy finds the obstruction: its minimum is 0 exactly when Φ ≡ 0. Abelian case only; re-checked here. | Active |
| [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) | A candidate structure is worth naming as a unit when its effect-to-noise ratio outruns the Occam cost of keeping it: reify when d'² exceeds the log prior-to-posterior variance ratio | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-160](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-160.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). By the Savage–Dickey ratio, ln BF(keep) = ½(d'² − Occam), so a direction, block or sector is real enough to name exactly when δ/ε > τ with τ² = ln(s²/σ²), the information the data added about it. In this record it prices the boundary tests for a combined form: a near-decomposable block ([LIT-905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-905.md)) earns a name when its gap beats its Occam factor. Re-checked here in the conjugate case. | Active |
| [CLAIM-155](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-155.md) | Willed agency is a kind between agency and selfhood: a control system whose behaviour is governed by a will-organization over several regimes is more than an agent and closer to a self, in the self-governing sense, without thereby being a subject | The owner's proposal of 2026-10-11, stated with the assistant. Agency can be had without will: a thermostat with its designers, or a training process. A control system that can properly be said to have a will is a narrower kind. It is the jurisdiction of a will-organization, and it is closer to a self in [ADR-024](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-024.md)'s self-governing sense, not in the subject sense. With [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) version 2, it answers the will paper's permissiveness objection on its merits. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md) | Mindfulness integrates a population of interests by changing which of them may act, not by changing what they value: noticing an impulse as an impulse suspends the step from its momentary dominance to its control of action, and leaves the discount curves as they were | The record's own conjecture, made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. It places mindfulness among [CLAIM-027](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-027.md)'s conditions of efficacy (suspension, accessibility), so it is a second individual-scale instance of that thesis. The one direct study read as summarised ([LIT-906](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-906.md)) points the other way, and the claim says so. It does not say mindfulness never changes valuation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md) v2 | Relative to a stated target, a combined form is one system while its joint dynamics are nearly decomposable with the form as a block whose gap beats the Occam factor, and it lasts as long as that block persists; the unit is the gap-isolated block, not any member | The record's proposed answer to [QUESTION-035](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md), joining the dual-filed MOM results. Simon's near-decomposability says what to compare: interaction inside a candidate block against interaction across its edge. The gap theorem says the unit is the block, and the Occam factor says when the gap is big enough to name it. Persistence is how long the block keeps clearing the threshold. It answers the owner's "privileged nomenclature" for the dancing couple with a test. Proposed: nothing has been measured. One-way drive passes, rightly (CLAIM-167), and the direction of coupling gives the system's architecture. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-158](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-158.md) | Systems differ in whether "who drives?" has an answer at a given level of description, and the kinds form a spectrum: fully top-down, bidirectional, emergent from the whole, and between | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11: "it's probably worth differentiating between systems where 'who drives?' has an answer wrt a particularly level of description or not. I think there's is probably a spectrum/gradient/distribution of kinds here." The record grounds it in the information decomposition ([LIT-025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-025.md)), whose downward-causation and causal-decoupling terms separate the kinds, and in proportional causation ([THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md)), which makes a higher level the cause system by system. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md) | The record's rival accounts of will are claims about drive profiles in different cells: Ainslie's interests are aggregate or emergent, the expected value of control is top-down, and will-organization is the maintained organization that governs how the drive profile changes | The assistant's reading, offered in chat on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's prompt. Ainslie's will has no governor: the person is "just the resultant" of bargaining interests, which is aggregate, or emergent if resolve is a property only the recursion has. The expected value of control posits a dedicated specifying system, which is top-down. The will paper's will-organization is the maintained organization of relations that decides which regime is effective, so it governs the drive profile's changes over time. That is the owner's point that "who drives" is not constant. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-160](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) | Data written for a potential future receiver has its intended meaning fixed by the write: even if it is never read, what it was meant to say was settled when it was stored | The owner's claim of 2026-10-11, in their words: "data is written with a potential future receiver in mind. even if the data is never read, its intended meaning was fixed by the write." It separates when identity is fixed (at the write, relative to a projected receiver) from when fidelity is measured (at a read, relative to an actual one), which the line had left unsettled. It does not say what a text means to a given reader is fixed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-161](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-161.md) | A system persists as the same self over an interval when a coherence measure is approximately conserved along its own trajectory, not merely matched by some map between its states | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-153](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-153.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The corpus's selfhood condition, that some map φ preserves a coherence score γ, is satisfied by any two systems with similar scores. Requiring the map to be the system's own evolution Φ_Δt makes selfhood approximate conservation of γ along the trajectory: γ is an approximate first integral, and the defect is a number. Proposed here because γ is unspecified. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) | Flow is intrapersonal synchronization: when an activity's immediate reward and its longer-run value coincide, no interest has to be overridden, and that is why focused action in flow is reported as effortless | The record's own conjecture, made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. It is grounded only weakly: the effort-cost account is a reading, and the flow literature is registered unread. It says that in flow there is nothing for will to do. It does not say flow is the best or the normal way to act as one. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-164](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-164.md) | What a spectral gap makes definite is the subspace of the cluster it isolates, not a single direction: the gap picks the object, and the object is a vector only when its own gap is wide | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-144](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-144.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). Under a perturbation δT, the subspace spanned by a cluster of singular values separated by a gap δ rotates by at most ‖δT‖/δ (Davis–Kahan), whatever happens to the vectors inside it. So the well-defined unit is the gap-isolated projector. Re-measured here. With [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) it is a criterion: the gap picks the object, and the Occam factor says whether the gap is big enough. | Active |
| [CLAIM-166](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-166.md) | "Who drives" is not constant: a person's drive profile changes over time, and a lower-level collective within the composite person, such as the gut microbiome, can at times drive higher-level behaviour and even experience | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11: "'who drives' isn't a constant. Considering myself as a multi-level agent, part of my composition is my microbiome ... that lower level collective is capable of influencing my higher level behavior and even phenomenological experience." The time claim is filed as the owner's. The microbiome claim is grounded in two reviews read the same day. The routes exist, and the effects are causal in rodents. The human evidence is modest: associations, small effects on subjective stress, and nulls. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-167](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-167.md) | One-way drive rightly passes the threshold criterion: a metronome and its musician, or a nerve and its muscle, form one system relative to a target that needs both, and the direction of coupling gives the system's internal architecture, not its membership | The owner's challenge to the open objection, 2026-10-11: "a metronome driving a musician, or a nerve driving a muscle, passes — and why shouldn't they?" Three reasons, set out by the assistant and accepted for filing by the owner. First, the objection repeats the coupling-constitution worry that [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) had already set aside: the criterion makes a new system, not parthood in the organism. Second, its intuitions are about agency, which [QUESTION-035](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-035.md) keeps apart. Third, whether a one-way driver is inside the block or an input is a choice relative to the target. Direction tells peers from hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-169](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-169.md) v2 | On Ainslie's account the population of interests is produced by desynchronized valuation, not given by a fixed architecture: an agent is many interests over a choice only as far as its valuations of that choice cross within the choice's horizon | The record's reading of [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md), made in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11. Interests are individuated by the delay at which each dominates, so where curves do not cross there is nothing to individuate them. The self's intertemporal multiplicity is then a variable, not a constant. It does not say that all multiplicity of self is intertemporal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md) v2 | The agents in a system are a factorization of it relative to a level of description and a target; agents in general are identified by adaptation, and willed agents are individuated by their will-organization: a willed agent is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The owner's thesis of 2026-10-11, stated in the record's terms after discussion. It is a collaboration, so it is not a quotation: "the agents in a given system are how we factorize that system relative to a given level of description", and agents are "identified by their will (and/or will-organization)". In the discussion, the owner chose will-organization over operative will, in the form "jurisdiction of a will-organization". Operative will flickers with the drive profile; a will-organization is maintained. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-172](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-172.md) v4 | Mutual entrainment is a sufficient mark of a combined form, and marks it as one of peers: when each side adjusts the other's timing the pair carries a collective variable neither has alone; one-way drive also makes a combined form, with a hierarchical architecture | The record's reading in answer to the owner's prompt of 2026-10-11, "connect extended self to entrainment". Clark & Chalmers' marks of extension are availability marks, and the coupling-constitution objection says coupling never makes parthood. Mutual entrainment sidesteps the objection rather than answering it: it individuates a new system by its collective variable. It does not cover a passive store like Otto's notebook, which is coupled across time by writing and reading, not by timing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) v2 | A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The assistant's admission test for the owner's thesis, filed at the owner's request. It has three tests on a candidate factor, at a level and for a target. (1) System: it clears the threshold criterion. (2) Description: a model in which it governs its own regimes for goals beats a device model by more than the Occam cost (Orseau et al., priced as in [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)). (3) Adaptation: its governance would change if its actions' consequences changed (Kenton et al.). It answers the circularity objection by running on candidates whose boundaries come from (1), not from agency, and it answers the permissiveness objection without the will paper's supposition. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-175](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-175.md) | A partner-dancing couple, while dancing, is one combined cognitive form on the extended-mind thesis's own terms, more clearly than Otto and his notebook, and merits a name of its own | The owner's reply of 2026-10-11 to the dancers objection, which they had not read: "under extended mind thesis, I'd argue that the pair, while dancing together, comprises a combined form that merits some privileged nomenclature of some kind". Clark & Chalmers endorse socially extended cognition, and the objection's own source calls the interaction an autonomous process. So the objection fails against the combined form and survives only as a question about selfhood. The name is not yet chosen. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-176](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md) v2 | Recurrence is the trigger of persistence this record is built around: coding a thing the second time it turns up captures exactly the drift that defeats an argument, and keeps capture from flooding the record | The filing rule of [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) ("a thing gets a code the second time it turns up"), read as one trigger of persistence ([CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md)), and the one this record is built around. Narrowed to that on 2026-10-11, on the owner's reframing. The same threshold appears in three places in luria and was found independently each time. Proposed: the rule has been applied, but no other threshold has been compared with it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) | An argument developed with collaborators who keep no memory fails at identity, not at structure: concepts are redefined silently, objections and readings come back as though new, and the thesis changes without anyone arguing for the change | Stated as a finding in [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md), from seven readers coding the will exchange, and found again in the What Survives Translation? exchange by the workbench reconstructions of 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10. Filed on 2026-10-11 as the first premise of the manuscript. Two exchanges with one owner and one assistant family, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-178](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-178.md) | A manuscript should be a view over the argument and not its only copy: a draft written straight from an exchange drops commitments and changes its thesis without saying so, and both become visible only against a record where claims carry status and inclusion separately | Luria's distinction between sources and generated views, carried over from files to argument. The evidence is the two "crystallized arguments" of the What Survives Translation? exchange and the manuscripts drafted from them (workbench 2026/10/09/025539, 2026/10/10/040457). Proposed: the record is kept beside the manuscript, and nothing generates a manuscript from it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-179](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-179.md) | When an agent does the filing, the cost of capturing argument falls on the party that would otherwise pay to re-derive it, which removes the disparity that design-rationale systems were abandoned over | The answer to the cautionary literature the owner filed before the argument schemes were built ([ADR-030](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-030.md)): design rationale goes uncaptured because whoever captures it is not whoever benefits. [ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) noted that agent filing changes the risk from capture stopping to capture flooding. This claim states why. Proposed: the record has run for one week. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-180](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-180.md) | Drift is retrieval failure outside a critical distance: a restatement close enough to an idea retrieves it, one that has drifted too far is taken for new, and a code bypasses retrieval by content altogether | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, when the owner raised sparse distributed memory and Hebbian learning after [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md), and filed at the owner's request. It reads the drift of [CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md) through SDM's critical distance (read in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md)) and Hopfield's basins of attraction (unread). The analogy is the claim; whether restatement distance predicts re-derivation has not been measured. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) | Storage is not anchoring, addressability is: a structure that is kept but cannot be pointed at part by part does not stop re-derivation, and the same content becomes an anchor once its parts get addresses | An answer to [QUESTION-038](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-038.md), proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11 and filed at the owner's request. The evidence is in the record already: the two shared transcripts persisted throughout, and ideas were re-derived inside them anyway. Their moves became citable only when the workbench reconstructions gave each turn a label. Two exchanges, and the comparison is not controlled, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-183](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-183.md) | Generated views of the record, fed back into the exchange, become instruments of the argument: they show where its terms evolved faster than its formalism | From U40 of the translation exchange, the first time a generated view went back into the conversation (workbench 2026/10/10/040455). The assistant read the term-revisions chain as evidence about the manuscript, and made five moves in reply. One of them was "Nucleation itself is a case study". One instance, so Proposed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) | The nucleation threshold of an argument is whatever makes a structure persist: a persistent structure is available as an anchor, and more complex structure can evolve only on anchors | The owner's reframing of 2026-10-11, after two readings showed that no physical nucleation threshold is a count. The threshold is not recurrence as such but whatever triggers persistence. Recurrence is the trigger this record is built around ([CLAIM-176](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-176.md)), and there are others. The readings fit the reframing: a physical nucleus is defined by persistence, and seeds that do not persist lose their power. Proposed: the generalization is stated, not tested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md) v2 | How fast an argument grows sets how it grows: drift tracks how fast new material arrives relative to how fast it is anchored, so a fast, prolific exchange branches, as a crystal grown far from equilibrium does, and a project memory stabilizes an argument by keeping anchoring up with arrival | Proposed by the assistant on 2026-10-11, while correcting its own crystal analogy ([CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md)), and filed at the owner's request rather than on a second occurrence. The analogy is to morphological instability. Near equilibrium a growing crystal faces over, and far from it the faces branch. The evidence so far is anecdotal. The fastest stretch of the translation exchange carried two moves of thesis, and drift has not been measured against pace. There is no slow exchange to compare it with, so the claim is Proposed and untested. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-187](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md) | Whether two systems compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the full admissible symmetry group and measuring what remains: a residual barrier marks a different mechanism, and a feature with no counterpart blocks the comparison | The record's one fully measured case of "factor out the admissible symmetries, then test what survives", which the pragmatic-transport line's questions about invariants under admissible transformation ([QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md), [QUESTION-029](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-029.md), [QUESTION-036](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-036.md)) ask for in the abstract. From five mode-connectivity THEORYs held without links to the line. The carry-over from trained networks to communicative kinds is the filer's, and is the claim's weak point. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-191](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) | Restating an argument across memoryless sessions is iterated transport with only a weak channel back to the source: without anchors, restatements drift toward the collaborators' own framings rather than at random, and a code restores continuity of transmission | The first claim joining the nucleating-argument and pragmatic-transport lines, which shared no edges. A sequence of memoryless sessions restating an argument is a chain of retellings, the telephone game of [CASE-015](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-015.md). The transport line's results then predict that drift has a direction, toward the transmitters' prior ([THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md), [CLAIM-090](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-090.md)), and that convergence is not preservation ([CLAIM-081](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md)). A code supplies [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission. Proposed from a synthesis review; the counter is [CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-192](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-192.md) | A multi-session argument's thesis can move without any participant arguing for the move, which is a case of an organized whole's course coming apart from its members' intentions | Links the nucleating-argument line to the distributed-agency line. The translation exchange's thesis moved from [CLAIM-017](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-017.md) to [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) to [CLAIM-133](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-133.md) with no turn arguing either move ([CLAIM-177](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-177.md)). [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) says an organized whole's operative intention can evolve apart from what its members intend. The owner, the assistant sessions and the record make up such a whole, and its thesis moved that way. [CLAIM-186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-186.md)'s test is an intervention test of both. Proposed from the synthesis review; the owner's memory and veto are the main reason to doubt it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md) | A linear probe family can tell apart only realizations whose representations differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed: any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst | A partial answer to [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) for the linear case, from four THEORYs the record held without linking them to the line. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)); kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed ([THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md)); an inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)); and spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). Proved results for learned representations; the carry-over to communicative realizations is the filer's. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-195](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-195.md) | For an argument, the constraint set that persistence is relative to is fixed by an amendable decision, not discovered: the record stipulates what counts as the same claim persisting, which makes the choice explicit without making it non-arbitrary | Files the point the workbench of 2026-10-11 (214308) left as notes on [CLAIM-185](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-185.md) and [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md). Viability is relative to a constraint set the theory does not supply ([THEORY-134](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md)), and the will-organization line leaves "who fixes the constraint set" open ([CLAIM-079](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-079.md), [ARG-007](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-007.md)). For an argument the record fixes it by decision ([ADR-032](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md) and its successors), so the set is explicit and amendable. That shows how one system fixes its set; it does not show the choice is non-arbitrary. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | A person's roles in contexts that do not meet cannot contradict one another: role conflict needs an overlap, which segregating audiences prevents and collapsed contexts create | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Roles in contexts that do not meet glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)), so contradiction between them is not yet a failure. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. They segregate audiences, which keeps the contexts disjoint, and they script the occasions where audiences must meet. Broadcast and networked media collapse contexts, which creates overlaps the person did not choose (boyd 2008, after Meyrowitz 1985). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) | Sections over contexts that do not overlap always glue, so a sense that differs between disjoint contexts is not a gluing failure: a failure needs an overlap carrying sections that disagree, and which families count as covers decides whether anything glues | Dual-filed from [MOM-CLM-088](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-088.md) ([ADR-037](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-037.md)). The sheaf condition says a family of sections that agree on overlaps glues to one global section. Where two contexts do not overlap, agreement is vacuous and they glue. So "tall", which takes one threshold for people and another for trees, is one global section with the comparison class part of the meaning, not a failure of gluing. A failure needs contexts that overlap and carry sections that disagree there. Which families count as covering is the piece that decides whether anything glues, and a sheaf picture of meaning that does not state it has decided nothing. | Active |
| [CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. If the windows do not overlap, the sections glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)): someone who prefers the diet in the morning and the cake at night is a time-indexed preference, not a divided self. Division needs an overlap, a choice on which both interests bear at once. On Ainslie's account that overlap is made by recursive self-prediction: the present choice is valued as a forecast of the later ones, so the later interest's valuation enters the present context. That is where intertemporal bargaining happens, and it is the coupling [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) | Blackwell's order bounds what a rendering makes possible for any receiver, and a given receiver's access is usable information relative to the rules it can apply, which a garbling can raise for that receiver but never above what the source makes possible | The record's reconciliation, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-225](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-225.md). Both standards are kept, in different roles: Blackwell's order is the ceiling, and [TERM-034](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-034.md)'s interpreter-relative fidelity ("relative to an interpreter and its available side information") is the receiver's. [CLAIM-087](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-087.md)'s improvement is a gain in usable information. The nearest held reading is [THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)'s "Its loss bounds r's best attainable risk for that problem from above", for restricted rules. The example is checkable; whether real receivers show such gains is a proposal. The usable-information literature is not held. It does not say which rule class real readers have. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) | Over a fixed scenario, a change of global compatibility at small local distortion needs contextual judgements, which the behavioural data read so far lack; the form of the headline those data leave open is a change of cover, in which a rendering makes some of the source's questions undecidable for its readers and decides others the source left open | The record's narrowing, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md) after [CLAIM-219](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-219.md). It concedes that the record's reading of [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) finds no contextual behavioural data, so the fixed-scenario form of "Translation may preserve local meanings while changing the global structure of meaning" has no case but a constructed one. It shows why the fixed-scenario form is sharp and why it needs contextuality. It keeps the form the record already names: "Only a change of scenario can make it jump" ([CLAIM-105](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-105.md)), and manuscript §11's "A transport may preserve overlaps but change the available measurement cover". A proposal; its test is the discriminating study. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md) | What the line adds to functional and relevance-theoretic accounts of translation is measured structure beyond a static pragmatic profile: the context-indexed profile, its response to later framings and its decision relevance predict receivers' recovery beyond the similarity of static stance and footing ratings | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md). [CLAIM-023](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-023.md) places the line's contribution in "a specified, testable account of which communicative distinctions a translation preserves", so the test of that contribution must be against the accounts that already hold the pragmatic point. This restores [CASE-005](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-005.md)'s three-way selection (semantic, static pragmatic and trajectory similarity), which was gone by A52, with human receivers. A proposal, untested. It does not say the functionalist rivals are wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) | A communicative kind's identity is grounded in its relational organization, for which competent participants' uptake is the standard; statistical methods recover aspects of it from restricted observations; translation transports it; and what persists is what the receivers can still recover, of which the analyst can certify the independently identifiable part | The record's restatement, on 2026-10-10, of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md) after the audit's objections to it ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md), [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md), [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md)). It keeps the four clauses, adds [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)'s standard to the first and [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md)'s reading to the fourth, and replaces the third defeat disjunct ("no relational structure beyond the observed response profiles is needed", which [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md) showed is always met or undecidable) with an observable comparison on transfer. Filed to complement [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md); whether it supersedes it is the owner's decision. A proposal, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-209](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-209.md) | Probes and statistical models recover only the distinctions identifiable from the relational evidence they are given, and a signature sufficient for a stated family of communicative decisions outside the observed probes can be identified when the full latent factorization is not | The assistant's second thesis at U62 (A240 T2), the positive answer to [QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md). It has now been asserted four times: A214 §7, A218 (RQ3 and the priority theorem target), A232 (§3.2 and F2) and A240. Filed with [QUESTION-027](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-027.md)'s scope: the unrestricted claim is answered by standard results, so its content is in decisions outside the observed probes. No signature is yet named. A proposal; the owner argued none of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-210](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-210.md) | Sharing a kind and being a rendering are different relations: kind-sharing is symmetric and says what is to be preserved, while fidelity belongs to a transport from a given source, so an utterance of the same kind made independently of the source shares its kind and has no fidelity to it | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-246](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-246.md). The October thesis puts fidelity in what persists "through those transformations", and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) makes fidelity the distortion profile of a transport. So the objection's independent utterance I shares the source's kind and has no fidelity to it, since no transport relates them; the translation T has both. Descent is a fact of provenance that the transport clause supplies, not something the kind criterion must recover. [CLAIM-002](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-002.md)'s continuity of transmission concerns the identity of a work, which [TERM-040](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md) keeps apart from the kind. Active, because it is read off the record's own texts. It does not say judges track descent. | Active |
| [CLAIM-212](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md) | Fidelity as a report and fidelity as a re-performance are different decision targets: Blackwell's order compares a rendering with its source as evidence about the source's situation, which both readers decide about, while a rendering that re-performs the act in the target's situation is compared only through a correspondence of situations | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md), which it reconciles rather than refutes. In report fidelity the parameter is the source's situation, common to both readers, so Blackwell's order is defined; the objection's worked case then gets a precise verdict, incomparability, as [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) expects, and a context-aware translator's non-garbling is compared by the order and quantified by [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md). The objection is right about re-performance, where [CLAIM-091](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-091.md)'s compensation lives: there a correspondence of situations is needed ([QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md)). For report tasks the task correspondence is the identity, which removes two of [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md)'s points there. A proposal; it does not say which kind of fidelity literary translation aims at. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-213](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-213.md) | A proposed relational kind is a hypothesis about invariance across admissible changes of measurement and context, not an equivalence class under the measurements now available, so realism about kinds gains empirical content as extrapolation to probe families, populations and environments not used to construct them | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12. The middle position it proposes between the realist reading of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s ontological clause and an operationalist one, which it would leave open as a tension rather than resolve. Proposed and not adopted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-214](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-214.md) | The distribution-over-situations criterion compares each language's own listener posterior, so it needs no correspondence of alternative sets; that a literal rendering can fail it is the criterion detecting a lost implicature, and a target language may admit no rendering that passes | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-236](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-236.md). [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md)'s criterion is P_o(z \| c_o, u_o) ≈ P_t(τ_z(z) \| c_t, u_t). On the rational-speech-act model each posterior is computed with its own language's alternatives, so comparing the posteriors needs no map between the alternative sets. The objection's worked case is right, and it shows the criterion rejecting a rendering that keeps the literal content and loses a scalar implicature. Active, because it is read off the criterion's form and checked by arithmetic. It does not say the model is right or that the criterion applies to poems. | Active |
| [CLAIM-215](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-215.md) | Communicative kinds are repeatable organizations of relations among participants, norms, commitments and possible consequences, which concrete events realize without being one another, and which kind an event realizes is not exhausted by the intrinsic properties of the expression token | The assistant's first thesis at U62 (A240 T1; A232's first proposition and §2), which splits the ontological clause of the October thesis ([CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)) out from the rest and narrows it. The owner asked how to update the theses and argued none of it. Its first two sentences are [TERM-040](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-040.md)'s definition. Its third is weaker than [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md): an intention-based account meets it too, so it does not tell relational constitution from that rival. The study cannot test it. A proposal. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) | For a communicative kind, the standard of sufficiency is the uptake of competent participants who know the standings and norms in play, so the judges are the criterion a probe family is tested against, and a kind outruns only the families coarser than that standard | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), and the argument [CLAIM-247](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) found missing. Calling a probe family insufficient ([CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), [CLAIM-135](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-135.md)) presupposes a standard beyond it. For an act partly constituted by uptake ([CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)), competent participants' uptake is that standard. The kind's extension is the class the standard fixes, and analysts' families are insufficient when coarser. No test needs a kind that outruns every family. A proposal, resting on a Proposed premise. It does not touch [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md)'s ontological clause, which the programme does not test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) | For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the audit's objections to the tests of the manuscript's thesis ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md)). It restates [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) as an empirical claim indexed to receivers and tasks, tested against the rival [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) itself names, a proposition with its force, on a behavioural criterion and with an interlingual arm that decides. Filed to complement [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md); whether it supersedes it is the owner's decision. It is a proposal, not a finding. It does not claim the line's distinctive machinery is needed: that is [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-223](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) | Whether a distinction survived is fixed by what the receivers can recover, and whether it can be shown to have survived is fixed by what the analyst's probes can identify, so the manuscript's thesis and the October fidelity clause, read so, answer different parts of one question | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-211](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-211.md), and the argument [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) asked for: "the thesis now needs both conditions, or an argument for dropping one". It keeps both, in different roles. On [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md)'s cases: a distinction identifiable but unusable did not survive for those receivers; one usable but unidentifiable survived without evidence of it. Read so, `complements` is right on content. A proposal: it is a reading of [CLAIM-139](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-139.md), not what A218 says. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md) v2 | Observational fidelity, as D_obs measures it, is a property of a rendering procedure over a class of source items, tested by one kernel family fitted on some items and scored on others, with the target term the readers' response averaged over the procedure's output; one source–target pair does not identify it, and a single rendering is judged as a sample of its procedure or by another measure | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of the manuscript's L_obs and the profile's D_obs after [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md), [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) and [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md). For one pair a constant kernel makes D_obs zero ([CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md)); fixed across items, it fits only if the target readers' responses do not vary with the item. The repair ties the outcome-level kernels to the text channel, makes the transport a property of a procedure ([CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md)), and makes deficiency a finite computation over judgement outcomes ([CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)). A proposal: the derivation is elementary, but whether the restated measure is informative is the defeat condition's empirical question. It does not say a fitted kernel is the translator's process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-231](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-231.md) | On observed responses, a rendering that keeps the response distribution of each order of two framings within ε of the source's, under an outcome correspondence, keeps the observed order effect within 2ε, a bound identified from data, while the intertwining identity bounds it only through defects of an unidentified state model | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-253](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-253.md). The commutator identity of the manuscript's §9 holds, and its defects are not identified from data, by the objection's hidden-bit construction. What can be estimated is the response distribution under each order, so the bound is restated on those: a special case of observational distortion with contexts indexed by framing order. Active, because it is elementary and checkable. It does not say the state-model account is wrong, and it does not identify the defects. | Active |
| [CLAIM-239](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-239.md) | A defeat condition that says something cannot be done is met by an argument that it cannot, not by a record of failures, so the admissibility and correspondence theses can fail by their own conditions, though no study the programme runs can make them fail | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the fourth point of [CLAIM-238](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-238.md). luria.yaml's blurb for `defeated_if` is "what would defeat the thesis — a kind of result or argument". [CLAIM-077](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-077.md)'s condition and [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md)'s second disjunct ("[QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) answered negatively") are met by a showing that the distinctions or correspondences cannot be fixed independently. What the objection gets right is that no finite study meets them, so the programme's experiments do not test these two theses; argument does. Active, because it is read off the rule. | Active |
| [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md) | A holistic fidelity judgement is fidelity under the judges' default task, a weighting of the profile's components that can be estimated on some renderings and tested on others, so it is well defined and consistent with task-relativity, and a defeat condition that uses it must name the population and fix the weighting before the test | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md). Task-relativity ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)) denies a ranking that holds across tasks, not that a population has a default task. A weighting estimated on held-in data and tested on held-out data is a finding, not a fit, and a weighting fixed before the test leaves no room to blame the task after a failure. A proposal: whether holistic judgements are such a weighting is itself empirical. The objection is right that the stated defeat conditions name neither task nor receivers; [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md), [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) and [QUESTION-075](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-075.md) address that. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-242](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-242.md) | The use-level counterpart of Saussure's value is an utterance's contrast with the alternatives its speaker could have used in context; values do not cross between languages, which is why fidelity is graded transport through an anchored correspondence rather than identity of value | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-254](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md). It grants the objection's premises: value is internal to one language state, and it is a fact of langue, while the line's observables are facts of use. It denies the conclusion. What the premise rules out is identity of value across languages, which the line does not claim ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)), and transport through a correspondence fixed from outside both systems is what [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s own qualification already requires. At the level of use, contrast with alternatives is the rational-speech-act model's premise ([THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)) and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's finding ([LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md)). Saussure becomes precedent, not premise. A proposal, not a refutation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) | What a developing argument should preserve through legitimate revision is its accountability structure, what was asserted, why, how it was challenged and what justified its revision, not its propositions, so fidelity is defined over justificatory and provenance relations while propositional content changes | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the third open tension ([CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) against [CLAIM-252](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md)). It reads the tension as mostly reconcilable and moves the fidelity object from propositions to justificatory relations. Proposed and not adopted. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-255](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-255.md) | Intending to perform an act, performing it and being recognized as having performed it are distinct, coupled variables: intended meaning is fixed at production, the act partly by roles, standing and norms, and recognition by uptake, so competent uptake is constitutive for some acts, evidential for others and irrelevant to the existence of still others | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the first open tension ([CLAIM-160](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) against [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)). It gives each claim its own object rather than picking one. Proposed and not adopted: the owner has not taken it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-257](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-257.md) | Observational distortion should be summed over the contexts both covers can host, with the target's new questions asked of the source too, and the questions only one side can decide reported as a separate change of cover, so that a rendering that adds a relation pays for it | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, after [CLAIM-256](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-256.md). D_obs sums over source contexts only, so a target context outside the image of τ is free. Asking the target's new question of the source, where its readers can answer it, puts it in both covers, and an addition then costs. Questions only one side can decide are a change of cover, which [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md) makes the line's headline; they are reported, not summed. A proposal: the restatement is a definition, and whether its added term predicts anything is the defeat condition. It does not say additions are distortions. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-259](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-259.md) | The decision term should be the positive part of the risk increase on the same decision problem, with losses in [0, 1] and a stated prior; so restated it is directed, counts no improvement as loss, and vanishes for every problem and prior exactly when the rendering is at least as informative as the source in Blackwell's order | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of A86's D_Q after [CLAIM-218](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-218.md). Define D⁺_Q(U → V; π) = sup over q in Q of [r_q,π(V) − r_q,π(U)]⁺, with r the Bayes risk under the prior π. It is directed and blind to improvement. With Q all finite problems and π all priors, it is zero exactly when V is at least as informative as U in Blackwell's order, by the Bayes form of Blackwell's theorem for finitely many states. A86's D_Q, with the identity on tasks, is its symmetrization. Under report fidelity ([CLAIM-212](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-212.md)) the paired task is the same task, so no scale between tasks is needed. The mathematics is checkable; the claim that this is the right decision term is a proposal. It does not say Q is fixed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-261](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-261.md) | Synchronization of an agent's interests is desirable, but not necessary for acting as one: internal conflict shows a human agent acting while its interests stay divided | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-078](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-078.md). A human agent who acts against a standing temptation acts as one agent while its interests stay divided, so synchronization is not what acting as one consists in. Synchronization is still better when it is available: nothing has to be overridden, and [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) says that is why flow is effortless. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-262](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-262.md) | Whether an agent's regimes are coordinated by discrete switches or by continuous reorganization depends on how the agent is constituted; both occur | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-079](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-079.md): both forms are possible, and which one an agent shows depends on its constitution. An agent made of a population whose choices accumulate like a drift-diffusion process reorganizes continuously. Twitch Plays Pokémon approximates one, best in democracy mode with the tally visible as votes arrive. The consequence for [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md)'s transition test is that it must be stated per constitution. A missing switch counts against coordination only in an agent built to switch. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-263](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-263.md) | Whether two trained networks compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the architecture's full symmetry group and measuring what remains: a barrier that survives alignment marks a different mechanism, connection after alignment means shared feature structure, and the test cannot run where features have no counterpart | The general content of [CLAIM-187](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md), filed alone in learned-structure under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md): a measured protocol for asking whether two trained solutions are the same solution. Quotient the full symmetry group, including the orthogonal map on a transformer's residual stream ([THEORY-112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md)). Read a barrier that survives as a difference of mechanism ([THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md)). Inside a basin, every layer's features interpolate ([THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)). The test cannot run where features have no counterpart ([THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md)) or the objectives share no structure ([THEORY-115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-115.md)). It is the first claim in the learned-structure line. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-264](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-264.md) | Two objects can agree on every probe in a restricted family without being isomorphic, so equivalence under a probe family is coarser than identity unless the family is rich enough, and only probes chosen independently of the comparison and evaluated on held-out cases are evidence that structure was preserved | The general content of [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that it does not rest on [CLAIM-046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-046.md) and [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), which are about pragmatic identity. The exact half: the restricted Yoneda functor is fully faithful exactly when the probe family is dense, and reflects isomorphisms when it is a strong generator; otherwise it identifies only up to a coarser equivalence. Matching every probe's marginal leaves the joint unconstrained. The evidential half: a family chosen to make two objects look alike is weak evidence that they share structure. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-265](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-265.md) | Local descriptions that disagree are not thereby incompatible: whether they obstruct a joint description can be decided only once the correspondence between their observations is fixed, and a correspondence fitted to remove the disagreement decides nothing | The general content of [CLAIM-143](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-143.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the order of tests does not rest on [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md), [CLAIM-004](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-004.md) and [CLAIM-035](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-035.md), which are about translation. Disagreement between local descriptions sorts into a coordinate difference, a structural transformation or a global obstruction, and the sort cannot be made until the transition maps are given. Inertial frames ([CASE-039](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-039.md)) show disagreement with no obstruction once the maps are known. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-266](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-266.md) | A family of probes that supplies an optimized system's training signal cannot also certify what the system preserves: optimization pushes toward whatever the probes reward, including what they cannot see, so preservation must be shown under probes not used to train it | The general content of [CLAIM-149](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-149.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that it does not rest on [CLAIM-011](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-011.md)'s account of correspondences in translation. Training against a probe family pushes a system toward whatever the family rewards, including differences it cannot see, so the family is not a certificate of what was preserved. [CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md) is a documented instance: a Projected FastGAN trained against ImageNet features matches StyleGAN2's FID, also computed in ImageNet features, while doing worse in CLIP space and with human judges. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-267](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-267.md) | Per-step discrepancies between a chain of maps and a reference chain compound through the sensitivity of the later steps, so the same local error can be damped, accumulated or amplified, and closeness at every step can coexist with large end-to-end divergence | The general content of [CLAIM-056](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-056.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the line-neutral recursion does not rest on [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s account of fidelity. It is elementary: with e_(i+1) ≤ L_i e_i + ε_i, the end-to-end error is bounded by the discrepancies weighted by the later Lipschitz constants. Three regimes follow. For stochastic kernels in total variation, contraction coefficients do not exceed one, so amplification needs another metric or a nonlinear, adaptive state. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-268](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-268.md) | Model stitching certifies an order of information only in its reconstruction form: a map fitted to reproduce the target layers shows the source representation is at least as informative for every decision on the label, task-loss stitching compares one decision problem through a fixed head, and a failure to stitch is no evidence against sufficiency | The general content of [CLAIM-126](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-126.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the result about stitching does not rest on [CLAIM-050](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-050.md)'s account of fidelity. Reconstruction-fitted stitching makes the target a garbling of the source given the label, which certifies one direction of Blackwell sufficiency ([THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md)). Task-loss stitching ([LIT-850](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-850.md)) compares one decision problem through a fixed head, orders neither representation, and is not invariant under reparametrisation. In both forms a failure says only that no map in the class works. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-269](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-269.md) | A regularized linear readout can tell apart only representations that differ in normalized kernel, and kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed, so any distinction beyond that is supplied by the analyst, not by the readouts | The general content of [CLAIM-193](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-193.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the linear result does not rest on [CLAIM-142](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-142.md), whose realist reading is about communicative identity. What a regularized linear readout decodes is a function of the normalized kernel ([THEORY-008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-008.md)). Kernels fix a representation only up to the symmetry of what is observed ([THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md)). An inner product beyond that is a stipulation ([THEORY-018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-018.md)). And spectral degeneracy does not identify the symmetry ([THEORY-019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-019.md)). These are proved results for learned representations. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-270](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-270.md) | Retaining information about where a Markov chain started and staying close to the starting distribution are different properties: a chain can forget its initial state while its distribution stays far from where it began, so convergence is not preservation and losing information about the origin is not degradation | The general content of [CLAIM-081](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md), filed alone under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md) so that the distinction does not rest, through [CLAIM-056](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-056.md), on [CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)'s account of fidelity. I(U_0; U_n) and D[P(U_n), P(U_0)] answer different questions. A contractive chain loses information about its initial state while converging to a stationary distribution that can be far from the start. The data-processing inequality bounds the first and says nothing about the second. | Proposed |
